he: וַיֹּֽאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־גָּד צַר־לִי מְאֹד נִפְּ֒לָה־נָּא בְיַד־יְהֹוָה כִּי־רַבִּים רַחֲמָיו וּבְיַד־אָדָם אַל־אֶפֹּֽלָה:

רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן חָטָֽאתִי לְפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה מָלֵא רַחֲמִים רַחֵם עָלַי וְקַבֵּל תַּחֲנוּנָי: יְהֹוָה אַל־בְּאַפְּ֒ךָ תוֹכִיחֵֽנִי וְאַל־בַּחֲמָתְ֒ךָ תְיַסְּ֒רֵֽנִי: חָנֵּֽנִי יְהֹוָה כִּי אֻמְלַל אָֽנִי רְפָאֵֽנִי יְהֹוָה כִּי נִבְהֲלוּ עֲצָמָי: וְנַפְשִׁי נִבְהֲלָה מְאֹד וְאַתָּה יְהֹוָה עַד־מָתָי: שׁוּבָה יְהֹוָה חַלְּ֒צָה נַפְשִׁי הוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי לְמַֽעַן חַסְדֶּֽךָ: כִּי אֵין בַּמָּֽוֶת זִכְרֶךָ בִּשְׁ֒אוֹל מִי־יוֹדֶה לָּךְ: יָגַֽעְתִּי־בְּאַנְחָתִי אַשְׂחֶה בְכָל־לַֽיְלָה מִטָּתִי בְּדִמְעָתִי עַרְשִׂי אַמְסֶה: עָשְׁ֒שָׁה מִכַּֽעַס עֵינִי עָתְ֒קָה בְּכָל־צוֹרְ֒רָי: סֽוּרוּ מִמֶּֽנִּי כָּל־פֹּֽעֲלֵי אָוֶן כִּי־שָׁמַע יְהֹוָה קוֹל בִּכְיִי: שָׁמַע יְהֹוָה תְּחִנָּתִי יְהֹוָה תְּפִלָּתִי יִקָּח: יֵבֽשׁוּ וְיִבָּהֲלוּ מְאֹד כָּל־אֹיְ֒בָי יָשֻֽׁבוּ יֵבֽשׁוּ רָֽגַע:
יְהֹוָה אֱלֺהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּֽךָ וְהִנָּחֵם עַל־הָרָעָה לְעַמֶּֽךָ:

הַבֵּט מִשָּׁמַֽיִם וּרְאֵה כִּי הָיִֽינוּ לַֽעַג וָקֶֽלֶס בַּגּוֹיִם: נֶחְשַֽׁבְנוּ כַּצֹּאן לָטֶֽבַח יוּבָל, לַהֲרוֹג וּלְאַבֵּד וּלְמַכָּה וּלְחֶרְפָּה: וּבְכָל־זֹאת שִׁמְךָ לֺא שָׁכָֽחְנוּ נָא אַל־תִּשְׁכָּחֵֽנוּ:
יְהֹוָה אֱלֺהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּֽךָ וְהִנָּחֵם עַל־הָרָעָה לְעַמֶּֽךָ:

זָרִים אוֹמְ֒רִים אֵין תּוֹחֶֽלֶת וְתִקְוָה: חוֹן אוֹם לְשִׁמְךָ מְקַוֶּה: טָהוֹר, יְשׁוּעָתֵֽנוּ קָרְ֒בָה, יָגַֽעְנוּ וְלֺא הֽוּנַח־לָֽנוּ: רַחֲמֶֽיךָ יִכְבְּ֒שׁוּ אֶת־כַּעַסְךָ מֵעָלֵֽינוּ: אָנָּא שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹנְ֒ךָ וְרַחֵם סְגֻלָּה אֲשֶׁר בָּחָֽרְתָּ:
יְהֹוָה אֱלֺהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּֽךָ וְהִנָּחֵם עַל־הָרָעָה לְעַמֶּֽךָ:

חֽוּסָה יְהֹוָה עָלֵֽינוּ בְּרַחֲמֶֽיךָ, וְאַל תִּתְּ֒נֵֽנוּ בִּידֵי אַכְזָרִים: לָֽמָּה יֹאמְ֒רוּ הַגּוֹיִם אַיֵּה־נָא אֱלֺהֵיהֶם לְמַעַנְךָ עֲשֵׂה עִמָּֽנוּ חֶֽסֶד וְאַל תְּאַחַר: אָנָּא שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹנְ֒ךָ וְרַחֵם סְגֻלָּה אֲשֶׁר בָּחָֽרְתָּ:
יְהֹוָה אֱלֺהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּֽךָ וְהִנָּחֵם עַל־הָרָעָה לְעַמֶּֽךָ:

קוֹלֵֽנוּ תִשְׁמַע וְתָחוֹן וְאַל־תִּטְּ֒שֵֽׁנוּ בְּיַד אֹיְ֒בֵֽינוּ לִמְחוֹת אֶת־שְׁמֵֽנוּ: זְכוֹר אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּֽעְתָּ לַאֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ, כְּכוֹכְ֒בֵי הַשָּׁמַֽיִם אַרְבֶּה אֶת־זַרְעֲכֶם וְעַתָּה נִשְׁאַֽרְנוּ מְעַט מֵהַרְבֵּה: וּבְכָל־זֹאת שִׁמְךָ לֺא שָׁכָֽחְנוּ נָא אַל תִּשְׁכָּחֵֽנוּ:
יְהֹוָה אֱלֺהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּֽךָ וְהִנָּחֵם עַל־הָרָעָה לְעַמֶּֽךָ:
עָזְ֒רֵֽנוּ אֱלֺהֵי יִשְׁעֵֽנוּ עַל־דְּבַר כְּבוֹד־שְׁמֶֽךָ וְהַצִּילֵֽנוּ וְכַפֵּר עַל־חַטֹּאתֵֽינוּ לְמַֽעַן שְׁמֶֽךָ:
יְהֹוָה אֱלֺהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּֽךָ וְהִנָּחֵם עַל־הָרָעָה לְעַמֶּֽךָ:
שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁמוֹר שְׁאֵרִית יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַל יֹאבַד יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאֹמְ֒רִים שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל:
שׁוֹמֵר גּוֹי אֶחָד שְׁמוֹר שְׁאֵרִית עַם אֶחָד וְאַל יֹאבַד גּוֹי אֶחָד הַמְיַחֲדִים שִׁמְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֺהֵֽינוּ יְהֹוָה אֶחָד:
שׁוֹמֵר גּוֹי קָדוֹשׁ שְׁמוֹר שְׁאֵרִית עַם קָדוֹשׁ וְאַל יֹאבַד גּוֹי קָדוֹשׁ הַמְשַׁלְּ֒שִׁים בְּשָׁלשׁ קְדֻשּׁוֹת לְקָדוֹשׁ:

מִתְרַצֶּה בְּרַחֲמִים וּמִתְפַּיֵּס בְּתַחֲנוּנִים הִתְרַצֶּה וְהִתְפַּיֵּס לְדוֹר עָנִי כִּי אֵין עוֹזֵר: אָבִֽינוּ מַלְכֵּֽנוּ חָנֵּֽנוּ וַעֲנֵֽנוּ כִּי אֵין בָּֽנוּ מַעֲשִׂים עֲשֵׂה עִמָּֽנוּ צְדָקָה וָחֶֽסֶד וְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ:

וַאֲנַֽחְנוּ לֺא נֵדַע מַה נַּעֲשֶׂה כִּי עָלֶֽיךָ עֵינֵֽינוּ: זְכֹר רַחֲמֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה וַחֲסָדֶֽיךָ כִּי מֵעוֹלָם הֵֽמָּה: יְהִי חַסְדְּךָ יְהֹוָה עָלֵֽינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר יִחַֽלְנוּ לָךְ: אַל תִּזְכָּר לָֽנוּ עֲוֹנוֹת רִאשׁוֹנִים מַהֵר יְקַדְּמֽוּנוּ רַחֲמֶֽיךָ כִּי דַלּֽוֹנוּ מְאֹד: חָנֵּֽנוּ יְהֹוָה חָנֵּֽנוּ כִּי־רַב שָׂבַֽעְנוּ בוּז: בְּרֺֽגֶז רַחֵם תִּזְכּוֹר: כִּי הוּא יָדַע יִצְרֵֽנוּ זָכוּר כִּי עָפָר אֲנָֽחְנוּ: עָזְרֵֽנוּ אֱלֺהֵי יִשְׁעֵֽנוּ עַל־דְּבַר כְּבוֹד־שְׁמֶֽךָ וְהַצִּילֵֽנוּ וְכַפֵּר עַל־חַטֹּאתֵֽינוּ לְמַֽעַן שְׁמֶֽךָ:
text: I Am Not Worthy, and We Are Not Worthy, but We Are Asking for Divine Favor Personally and Nationally

For a list of when Tachanun is omitted, see Appendix 12:9. There is a very tricky and delicate balance needed in proper, healthy avodas Hashem, which is reflected in our tefillos. On one hand, we need to admit (to Hashem and to ourselves!) that we have made mistakes and are not completely living up to our potential. In terms of strict justice and the letter of the law, we are not really worthy of all the bounty that Hashem gives us. There are even times that we use His gifts against Him! And that is the major focus of Tachanun. But on the other hand, the goal of saying Tachanun is not to give up and say, “OK—so I’m just a big loser—forget it!” As we explained earlier, by Modeh Ani—clearly Hashem believes in you! He woke you up. He believes you are important and that you CAN correct your mistakes in order to reach greater heights! But if you avoid confronting your mistakes and tell yourself, “I’m doing just fine and I have nothing to improve,” you’ll never aspire to be the greatest “you” you can be. Be honest about your faults, and then believe in yourself as much as Hashem believes in you! “Long Tachanun” (only on Mondays and Thursdays) On all other weekdays, begin with "Short Tachanun" on page 87. Why Mondays and Thursdays? These two days are considered “ favorable days,” since Moshe went up to Har Sinai on a Thursday (the first of Elul) to get the second set of Luchos and came down forty days later on a Monday (on Yom Kippur itself) with the second set of Luchos. Since they are auspicious days, we add in these seven paragraphs of Tachanun.

What is the theme? These seven paragraphs were written by different sages and eventually were put together to form the “long Tachanun,” which is why you will find that many of the ideas and themes repeat themselves. The basic theme is that Hashem is our only hope for salvation from the suffering that we have brought upon ourselves through not living up to our mission to the world. As contrasted with the “short Tachanun,” which is personal in nature (and said every weekday), the “long Tachanun” focuses on our communal pain, and the desecrated status of Yerushalayim, our holy city. Since the wording of the seven paragraphs of “long Tachanun” is quite straightforward and understandable, we will simply point out the key themes of each paragraph.

We admit that it is because of our own sins that we, Your nation, and Your holy city Yerushalayim have become an object of scorn among the nations (which is a huge chillul Hashem). We ask that You save us and Your city in the merit of our ancestors and because Your kindness is eternal.
85 Shacharis • Tachanun

See our desolation and the desolation of Your city Yerushalayim. Though all of that is our own fault, still, if Your nation would perish and if Your city would fall, then the nations of the world would say, “Where is their God?” which would be a huge chillul Hashem! Therefore, please save us and rebuild Yerushalayim so that everyone will recognize You and Your providence.
Save us and have compassion on us in the merit of the ) You made to the Avos( promise that we would be Your eternal nation.
Do not forsake us and do not be far away from us; see all that we have suffered throughout our history. Save us in the merit of the Bris Bein Habesarim and in the merit of Akeidas Yitzchak.

We will examine our actions, try to improve, and return, Please forgive our sins and save us from all our troubles and sorrows, for You are full of mercy and compassion. The world knows we are Your nation, and the nations recognize!Your power by what happens to us
to You for You, Hashem, are always open to accepting our teshuvah. Help us achieve our teshuvah and save us from our troubles, for it is only You, Hashem, that we turn to for help.
87 Shacharis • Tachanun

Though we have not lived up to our potential, please remember the bris with the Avos and our daily proclamations of the Shema, which is our acceptance of You as our only God. Have mercy on Your land and on Your children, and show Your power over Your enemies. And show favor to us, the nation who, with constant love, proclaim twice a day: שׂ!
“Short Tachanun” (Every Weekday:

As David HaMelech said to the prophet Gad: I accept the fact that I have sinned and must be punished, but please, let my punishment come directly from Hashem Himself, since He is merciful, rather than through the hands of humans.

I know I have sinned, but I ask, please, Hashem, do not punish me “out of anger,” but rather with love, in a way that Your punishments will help me see my mistakes and be a catalyst to correct them! At times, I feel so weighed down with troubles and with a feeling that I have missed opportunities and not lived up to my potential! But I am confident that You will accept my tefillah, give me opportunities to improve, and rid me of my difficulties, so that I can grow and serve You to my fullest potential which is why You put me here on earth!
On Mondays and Thursdays (when the “long Tachanun” focuses on our communal suffering and pain), add the following; on other days, continue on page 90.

( As Moshe said to Hashem after the sin of the golden calf, when asking Him to forgive Bnei Yisrael) Hashem, turn back from Your fierce anger; and soften the harsh punishment You intended to inflict on Your people. We now describe our nation’s state of suffering each followed by the above plea (, ) that Hashem should soften His punishment of us.

We are despised by the nations of the world and are viewed as sheep to be led to the slaughter, to be killed and humiliated. And yet, despite this, we have not forgotten You and Your laws; please do not forget us! …
89 Shacharis • Tachanun
The world says Bnei Yisrael have no future! But we place our hope with You that Your compassion will suppress Your anger against us. …
The hostile masses treat us with cruelty, and they gloat, saying, “Where is their God?” For the glory of Your name, deal kindly with us. …

Do not leave us in the hands of our enemies who want to wipe us out! Remember Your promise to the Avos that we would be as numerous as the stars, yet now we are only a small group among the nations of the world. And yet despite this, we have not forgotten You and Your laws; please do!not forget us …
Save us and pardon our sins, for it is through our miraculous survival in history that the!world recognizes Your power …
On all days we continue here:
You are the guardian of Yisrael; do not let Yisrael perish in the merit that we say daily!
You are the guardian of the one and only unique nation; do not let that one and only unique nation perish in the merit that we say daily that Hashem is!
You are the guardian of the separate and elevated nation; do not let that separate and elevated nation perish in the merit that we (like the angels) declare daily!
There is no power that can save us but You. Though we may not be worthy, deal with us with Your loving-kindness and chessed.

( To sum it all up:) Hashem, we do not know what else we can do, so we turn to You for Your kindness and help. We know we lack merit, but You know that we are material beings and thus have many struggles! Pardon us and give us another chance to prove ourselves, so that we may spread the knowledge of Your Presence to the whole world.

( The, person saying Kaddish proclaims our hope that) soon, in our lifetime, the entire world, which Hashem: created precisely according to His. Will, will recognize Hashem as,, the Source of all and will see the,

sanctity, perfection, and purpose,,. of all He has done.. ( ( We all enthusiastically, ) respond:) Absolutely correct!:, May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that all His actions are great and deserving of praise! ( The person saying Kaddish then points out that) in reality, the true greatness and power of Hashem far exceeds any praises that we mere humans could say. And to that we respond: Absolutely correct!

Now Let’s Learn Some Torah! Everyone should learn Torah every day each at their own level! In addition to this, a public reading of the Torah was established for Mondays and Thursdays as a mini “reenactment” of Maamad Har Sinai, so that we may reaffirm the Torah as being our guide not only personally but also nationally. Taking Out the Torah
Said on Mondays and Thursdays when Tachanun was recited::

( As we take out the Torah, we proclaim that) we know that we have not fulfilled everything that it says in Your Torah, but please, in Your lovingkindness, do not rebuke us. Instead, forgive us, and help us see Your Presence in the world.
When the Aron traveled (leading Bnei Yisrael through the desert), Moshe requested that all our enemies and those who hate us should run away in fright!,

( So too, when the Beis Hamikdash will be rebuilt, all the nations of the world will come to Yerushalayim to learn the truth and will proclaim:) “Torah comes out of Zion (to light up the entire world) and Hashem’s truth comes (only) from Yerushalayim!” We thank You, Hashem, for giving us Your Torah and trusting us with the responsibility (now even before Mashiach comes) to spread its truth everywhere (by our actions and words).
A tefillah from the Zohar, based on the idea that when the aron kodesh is open, it is an auspicious time to make requests

Hashem, You are the Source of everything! Please redeem us, rebuild the Beis Hamikdash, shine Your light on us, and accept all our tefillos. May we all live long and happy lives. Protect me, all that is mine, and all that belongs to all of Bnei Yisrael. You feed all, You sustain all, You rule over all and I am Your servant, who bows before Your glorious Torah! I do not put my trust in humans or in angels, but rather, I place my complete trust in You, for You are the One True God, Whose Torah and Prophets are all true, and Whose actions are all good and true! Please, open my heart to Your Torah! And fulfill all that I and all Your nation Yisrael wish for but only if what we wish for is really good for us and will give us life and peace!

( Holding the Sefer Torah, the chazzan calls out:) Declare the greatness of Hashem with me; and together we will praise Him! ( And we respond:) Any power, victories, or glory that we have been granted are really all Yours, because everything is really Yours! The kingship and rule of leaders (here on earth) derive from You! Therefore, we praise You and bow ourselves before You. Our merciful Father, have mercy on us, help us in fulfilling our mission and protect us from the yetzer hara, and fulfill our requests so we may dedicate ourselves to serving You.
Reading the Torah
( When calling up the,: first aliyah the gabbai proclaims:) May the sovereignty of Hashem: over us as His special nation be. revealed to all soon, and may
Hashem show loving-kindness to: us. Everyone should praise Hashem::

and show honor to His Torah, but specifically, let (name, son of father’s name) come forward. We all thank You, Hashem, for giving Your Torah to Bnei Yisrael. ( And everyone declares together: As Moshe told the Jews who had resisted the temptation to worship the idol Baal-Pe’or) and all of you who stood firm and remained close with Hashem; you are all alive today (you merit Divine protection in this life, you merit eternal life, and you live lives of meaning that make a lasting impression on the world).

textBlocks.text: I Am Not Worthy, and We Are Not Worthy, but We Are Asking for Divine Favor Personally and Nationally

For a list of when Tachanun is omitted, see Appendix 12:9. There is a very tricky and delicate balance needed in proper, healthy avodas Hashem, which is reflected in our tefillos. On one hand, we need to admit (to Hashem and to ourselves!) that we have made mistakes and are not completely living up to our potential. In terms of strict justice and the letter of the law, we are not really worthy of all the bounty that Hashem gives us. There are even times that we use His gifts against Him! And that is the major focus of Tachanun. But on the other hand, the goal of saying Tachanun is not to give up and say, “OK—so I’m just a big loser—forget it!” As we explained earlier, by Modeh Ani—clearly Hashem believes in you! He woke you up. He believes you are important and that you CAN correct your mistakes in order to reach greater heights! But if you avoid confronting your mistakes and tell yourself, “I’m doing just fine and I have nothing to improve,” you’ll never aspire to be the greatest “you” you can be. Be honest about your faults, and then believe in yourself as much as Hashem believes in you! “Long Tachanun” (only on Mondays and Thursdays) On all other weekdays, begin with "Short Tachanun" on page 87. Why Mondays and Thursdays? These two days are considered “ favorable days,” since Moshe went up to Har Sinai on a Thursday (the first of Elul) to get the second set of Luchos and came down forty days later on a Monday (on Yom Kippur itself) with the second set of Luchos. Since they are auspicious days, we add in these seven paragraphs of Tachanun.

What is the theme? These seven paragraphs were written by different sages and eventually were put together to form the “long Tachanun,” which is why you will find that many of the ideas and themes repeat themselves. The basic theme is that Hashem is our only hope for salvation from the suffering that we have brought upon ourselves through not living up to our mission to the world. As contrasted with the “short Tachanun,” which is personal in nature (and said every weekday), the “long Tachanun” focuses on our communal pain, and the desecrated status of Yerushalayim, our holy city. Since the wording of the seven paragraphs of “long Tachanun” is quite straightforward and understandable, we will simply point out the key themes of each paragraph.

We admit that it is because of our own sins that we, Your nation, and Your holy city Yerushalayim have become an object of scorn among the nations (which is a huge chillul Hashem). We ask that You save us and Your city in the merit of our ancestors and because Your kindness is eternal.
85 Shacharis • Tachanun

See our desolation and the desolation of Your city Yerushalayim. Though all of that is our own fault, still, if Your nation would perish and if Your city would fall, then the nations of the world would say, “Where is their God?” which would be a huge chillul Hashem! Therefore, please save us and rebuild Yerushalayim so that everyone will recognize You and Your providence.
Save us and have compassion on us in the merit of the ) You made to the Avos( promise that we would be Your eternal nation.
Do not forsake us and do not be far away from us; see all that we have suffered throughout our history. Save us in the merit of the Bris Bein Habesarim and in the merit of Akeidas Yitzchak.

We will examine our actions, try to improve, and return, Please forgive our sins and save us from all our troubles and sorrows, for You are full of mercy and compassion. The world knows we are Your nation, and the nations recognize!Your power by what happens to us
to You for You, Hashem, are always open to accepting our teshuvah. Help us achieve our teshuvah and save us from our troubles, for it is only You, Hashem, that we turn to for help.

I know I have sinned, but I ask, please, Hashem, do not punish me “out of anger,” but rather with love, in a way that Your punishments will help me see my mistakes and be a catalyst to correct them! At times, I feel so weighed down with troubles and with a feeling that I have missed opportunities and not lived up to my potential! But I am confident that You will accept my tefillah, give me opportunities to improve, and rid me of my difficulties, so that I can grow and serve You to my fullest potential which is why You put me here on earth!

Now Let’s Learn Some Torah! Everyone should learn Torah every day each at their own level!
